If I visit some webpages with an ad-blocker, only the ads are blocked. But in others, the site blocks the whole thing. Does that mean the site knows even its contents are ads?
Some sites detect ad blockers and have taken to blocking their content from those using an ad blocker.

Yep. Yahoo seems to be the big one with me, their site and affiliated sites come in either covered by a big blank banner i cant remove or garbled junk. Sok i dont like them anyways and can get better service elsewhere.

Does that mean the site knows even its contents are ads?

Usually, it's one of these:

  1. Site serves ads from the same domain as it serves the rest of it's content; no way to filter just the ads, so the site breaks. Poor design.

  2. Site is explicitly looking to see if the ads are blocked, and refusing to load if they are. Malicious design.

  3. Site unintentionally depends on advertisements having loaded (e.g. Start video after ad says it's done), and so will not load if they're blocked. Poor design.

  4. Site (or key dependencies) is unknown to your ad blocker, so it doesn't know to let it through. Your/blocker's fault.

Nature is not an intelligent being, it is just a set of basic laws on which we, biological beings, survive. So far changes in our DNA have been completely accidental, then the said set of rules "decided" which of these changes were "compatible" with life. This doesn't always work, sometimes useful changes are lost by pure chance and useless or dangerous changes manage to spread. This is the case for instance with genetic diseases. This kind of evolution requires hundreds of thousands of years to work, and the reason it takes so much is that it is driven by chance.

We now have the knowledge and means to change it and shape our own future. It is a long time now that we don't follow anymore the rules of Nature, and this isn't necessarily a bad thing. Think for instance to severely handicapped persons... they would just die if left alone with the rules of Nature. But we don't let this to happen because we don't like it and this, in turn, has the potential to damage our species by letting "wrong" genes to spread... genes that wouldn't survive long enough to spread in Nature.
